deterministic.name: check-verifier-contract.py
deterministic.evidence: Manual application with cited source/local probes. bash -n tests/test.sh exits0 and no CR/shell exec exists. Source writes zero at:60, traps cleanup:61, probes before RewardKit and stages both suites. Nevertheless unchanged shared restart code :152-180 sends only SIGTERM and can accept the old listener after5 seconds, while cleanup:33-39 has an unbounded wait. Verified local/shared-harness/results.json and its exact witness script/logs: restart_app isError=false, old_pid=7, recorded_new_pid=68, answering_pid_after=7; replacement crashes EADDRINUSE and helper logs ready=1. Full unchanged entrypoint with a no-provider failing CLI stub remains running after12.0045 seconds with fixture PID95 answering. It does preserve the initial zero, but does not complete safely and can falsely attest a restart.
deterministic.counterexample: A submitted in-memory app registers a SIGTERM handler and continues serving. The actual fixture preserves its old PID across restart_app, while the replacement fails to bind and the tool reports successful process replacement. Such an app can appear durable without being restarted. A valid app using a graceful shutdown longer than five seconds is also not forbidden by the public runtime contract. At final cleanup the same handler leaves test.sh waiting indefinitely until an outer termination.
deterministic.suggested_fix: Escalate the demonstrated defect for an authorized shared-template fix: bounded TERM then KILL/reap, verify old process death and replacement PID liveness, and bound final cleanup; freeze and rerun after the approved canonical update rather than patching task-local harness code.

challenge_analysis.broken_app: A server-backed-looking app that keeps all records in memory and ignores SIGTERM could preserve the same records across the supposed restart. The raw fixture demonstrates the decisive mechanism: restart_app returns isError=false while old PID 7 still answers and new PID 68 fails EADDRINUSE. This is actual helper behavior; an end-to-end grade of that in-memory app was not run.
challenge_analysis.conforming_alternative: A conforming app with ordinary graceful SIGTERM handling that takes longer than five seconds has no public shutdown deadline. The helper can report success from its old listener before replacement. A conforming app whose browser MCP fails also lacks an explicit honest-missing-evidence policy in render/visual; the resolved prompts cannot distinguish that evaluator failure from an observed gate failure. These are concrete counterexamples from source plus the TERM-resistant fixture, not a claimed model score.
challenge_analysis.positive_controls: Local score.py probes returned gate failure=0, gates-only=0, all dimensions one=1, weighted partial=.5, exact functional floor=.05 =>0, and rejected bool/NaN. The constraints rubric demands fresh unique UI saves and independent Auditor readback, so a plain static seed page is explicitly insufficient.
